narrative: The model estimated a 65.9% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt, so your application was denied because the review treated that risk as too high. Your middle family-income bracket was the third-most influential factor and added further weight toward the failure prediction; accepted students were more often from upper-middle-income backgrounds, while middle-income students made up a smaller share. Your undergraduate GPA of 3.70, above the accepted average of 3.23, was a positive signal, but it was not enough to overcome the leading concerns. To improve your chances, focus on raising your admissions test score through structured preparation and consider retaking it.
